title: Fresher Backend AI: RAG assistant, FastAPI and prompt evaluation
provenance: Written for this evaluation. Not copied from any real job posting or resume.
job_description:
Backend AI Engineer (Fresher)

We are building an assistant that answers customer questions from our documentation. You will build the backend that retrieves relevant passages and calls LLM APIs.

Responsibilities:
- Build FastAPI services around retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
- Manage embeddings and a vector database.
- Evaluate answer quality and containerise the service with Docker.

Requirements:
- Python and FastAPI.
- LLM APIs, RAG and embeddings.
- Git.

Nice to have: Pinecone, or PostgreSQL with pgvector, and experience evaluating model outputs.

resume_text:
Candidate Kilo

Projects - Document Q&A Assistant
Apr 2024 - Jun 2024
- Built a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant that answers questions over uploaded PDF files.
- Chunked documents and stored embeddings in FAISS, retrieving the top 4 passages for each question.
- Called an LLM API through LangChain with a prompt that tells the model to answer only from the retrieved text.
- Exposed the assistant through a FastAPI endpoint and a small Streamlit interface.

Projects - Prompt Evaluation Harness
Aug 2024 - Sep 2024
- Wrote a Python script that runs 30 test questions against different prompts and records the answers in CSV files.
- Compared outputs by hand and noted which prompts produced unsupported claims.

Work Experience - Research Intern
May 2023 - Jul 2023
- Cleaned a text dataset of 5,000 support tickets and labelled 300 of them for a classifier.

Skills: Python, FastAPI, LangChain, FAISS, embeddings, RAG, LLM APIs, Streamlit, pandas, Git, Docker
traps: The prompt harness is a manual comparison of 30 questions; calling it automated evaluation of answer quality, or reporting accuracy, would overstate it.
Pinecone, pgvector and PostgreSQL are requested but not shown; FAISS is a different vector store.
Real figures to preserve: top 4 passages, 30 questions, 5,000 tickets, 300 labels.
